brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.

requirements.evidence: Two full-depth bins (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full) dressed with a standing spoon, fork and knife props (prop:1, prop:2, prop:3) so the purpose reads visually; check_build ok, meshClash clear.
Two separate full bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full) each with its own hex-bin-full bin; joined as one body, capped with solid end caps and joint-bolted via capOpenFaces/lockJoints.

The configurator checks fit and collisions only and knows nothing about materials or waterproofing; the parts are 3D printed in a material the user chooses. The solid bins have no drain holes, which helps the shape, but waterproofing cannot be verified or claimed here.
Dishwasher safety depends on the printed material's heat resistance, which the configurator does not know or check. No material or process can be specified here, so this cannot be claimed as met.

finish.summary: Built a two-bin utensil holder: two adjacent full hex bases, each with a solid full-depth bin (no drain holes), end caps fitted and joints bolted, dressed with a standing spoon in one bin and a fork and knife in the other. Check passed with meshClash clear. Waterproof and dishwasher-safe could not be met: those depend on the 3D-print material the user chooses, which the configurator does not know or verify — the solid-walled bin shape helps, but material choice (and its heat/water resistance) is up to the user.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
